items.stem: Why use millis() instead of delay() for timing multiple tasks in a sketch?

options.text: delay() blocks all other code, while millis() lets the loop keep running and handle several tasks
options.rationale: Correct: non-blocking timing keeps the program responsive.

options.text: millis() is less accurate than delay()
options.rationale: millis-based timing is generally preferred for multitasking.

options.text: delay() uses no CPU at all
options.rationale: delay() blocks the CPU from other work.
It does not block the loop.

items.explanation: Correct: non-blocking timing keeps the program responsive.

items.stem: Why should a small motor usually be driven through a transistor or driver rather than directly from an Arduino pin?

options.text: A logic pin cannot supply enough current and the motor's inductive load can damage the microcontroller
options.rationale: Correct: a driver handles the current and protects the MCU.

options.text: Motors require no current to run
A pin outputs AC suitable for motors

options.rationale: A driver enables, not slows, the motor.

items.explanation: Correct: a driver handles the current and protects the MCU.

items.stem: Which statements about reading inputs on an Arduino are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: A digital input left unconnected can float, so a pull-up or pull-down resistor is used
options.rationale: Correct: pull resistors give a defined logic level.

options.text: A mechanical button can bounce, registering multiple transitions per press
options.rationale: Correct: debouncing filters out the bounce.

options.text: analogRead returns a true analog voltage, not a number
options.rationale: False; it returns a digitised integer from the ADC.

options.text: Floating inputs always read a stable LOW

items.explanation: Correct: pull resistors give a defined logic level.; Correct: debouncing filters out the bounce.
